newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CSR says housing slump hit first half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CSR says housing slump hit first half.

text.p: CSR Ltd said on Monday that weak Australian housing and aluminium markets were the main reasons for the fall in profits for the six months ended September 30 despite a strong performance from the United States.

"Continuing strong performance from CSR America and a good first half year performance by our sugar milling business were not able to offset weaker results in all Australian building products businesses and aluminium," CSR said.
CSR earlier reported a 24 percent fall in net profit before abnormals to A$154.7 million in the six months to September 30.
CSR said its U.S. unit, CSR America, reported a record six months profit of A$78.5 million, 13 percent up on the same period a year earlier.
"Demand levels in most of our markets in North America increased slightly on last year," the company said.

Sugar profits rose 41 percent to A$54.1 million despite lower raw sugar prices. The profit rise was due to a return to normal weather conditions in Queensland during the sugar milling season and a good performance at the sugar mills, CSR said. It said intense competition again affected refined sugar profits.

CSR said net profits before abnormals from its Australian building materials businesses dropped to A$43.0 million in the first half from A$91.6 million a year earlier. Low prices affected all domestic building market sectors, it said.
Housing demand fell, with the number of building starts fell 19 percent compared with the same period last year, CSR said.
It said timber profitability was especially hard hit in the Australian market where suppliers, including CSR, with recently expanded production capacity met stiff competition from imports.
CSR said the net profit for its aluminium unit fell 28 percent to A$29.00 million in the half, due to lower prices.
CSR said it made progress in the efficiency and restructuring of its operations, with the lowering of working capital and overhead costs, and in generating cash from its operations.
It said 18 Australian plants were closed in the half, reducing employment by 350. The sale of properties and plant raised A$139 million.
A further 35 sites in Australia and 17 in the United States are being actively marketed.

"These improvements moderated the effect on CSR's profits of the fall in prices in virtually every Australian market we supply. By the end of the period, price increases had been achieved for some key products in selected markets," it said.
CSR said its recent capital expansion phase is now largely complete.
At 2.15 p.m. (0315 GMT), CSR shares were four cents lower at A$4.24.
